correctness.rationale: The recursive block sampler is exactly uniform because a prescribed first block/order and recursively prescribed remainder have product probability 1/R!. Conditional on prior blocks, each block is a uniform critical-size subset of the residual system, so the source theorem applies with its polynomial failure bound. A prefix through N/2 meets at most 1+2^(2/p)mN^(-2/p) blocks; Minkowski and coefficient Cauchy–Schwarz give the required K_p scale, and a union bound over O(N^(1-2/p)) blocks makes all such prefixes good simultaneously. For later prefixes, L2/Linfinity interpolation gives K_p(T)<=|T|^((1-2/p)/2), which is on the same scale when m>N/2. The Fourier near-origin interval supplies the matching lower bound. The complete corrected RESULT.md preserves this proof and changes only malformed escape/control characters.

final_claim: For every bounded orthogonal system and p>2, one uniformly random permutation has, with arbitrary polynomially high probability, K_p on every prefix m simultaneously bounded on the sharp scale max(1,sqrt(m)N^(-1/p)); the Fourier system forces that same order for every m-element subset.
